# Size-adjusted connectivity

Raw rankings of `ECS_pct` across all regions are dominated by size
effects: small regions score well on ratio metrics almost by
construction (the top ranks by raw `ECS_pct_59` are tiny villages). A
fair comparison of cities needs to control for size first: fit `ECS_pct`
as a function of `log(total_area_ha)` across all regions, then use the
residual (observed minus size-predicted) as the comparison metric, as
when comparing observed with island-biogeography-predicted species
richness.

```{r fit_residual_models}
library(ggplot2)
if (!requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggrepel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(ggrepel)

# Defined here as well as in the national_loop chunk, so the analysis and
# figure chunks below can be run without re-running the national build.
results_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "08_national_ecs_results.csv")

results <- read.csv(results_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ok <- results |> filter(is.na(error), total_area_ha > 0)
ok$log_area <- log(ok$total_area_ha)

fit_residuals <- function(pct_col) {
  sub <- ok |> filter(!is.na(.data[[pct_col]]))
  fit <- lm(reformulate("log_area", response = pct_col), data = sub)
  sub$predicted <- predict(fit)
  sub$residual <- sub[[pct_col]] - sub$predicted
  list(data = sub, fit = fit)
}

res_59 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_59")
res_99 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_99")
res_512 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_512")

cat("ECS_pct_59 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_59$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("ECS_pct_99 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_99$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("ECS_pct_512 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_512$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
```

# SLOSS: does connectivity, not area, resolve the debate?

The classic SLOSS ("Single Large Or Several Small") question asks whether
the same total habitat area is better conserved as one large reserve or
several small ones. This tests it directly: find real regions with
near-identical total woodland area and check whether the number of
separate physical patches (`n_patches`) explains the difference in
outcome.

The analysis uses `n_patches`, not `nClusters_*`: nClusters is a property
of the same thresholded graph that ECS is computed from, so "fewer
clusters, higher ECS" is close to true by construction. n_patches is
counted from the raw raster before any threshold is applied and has no
such relationship to the ECS formula.

## Formal test: does fragmentation explain connectivity beyond area alone?

```{r sloss_formal_test}
# Tests whether fragmentation (log_patches) explains connectivity beyond
# area alone, and whether the residuals show spatial autocorrelation that
# a spatial smooth term should absorb.
#
# Uses n_patches (physical patch count from the raw raster, before any
# threshold is applied), not nClusters_* (post-threshold cluster count).
# nClusters is a property of the same thresholded graph that ECS is
# computed from: fewer clusters mechanically raises sum(cluster_area^2)
# for a fixed total area, so "fewer clusters, higher ECS" would be close
# to true by construction rather than an independent finding.
#
# Moran's I is computed directly from its definition
# (I = (n/S0) * sum_ij w_ij z_i z_j / sum_i z_i^2) rather than through an
# extra package. Significance is by permutation (999 shuffles of the
# residuals across locations), which needs no distributional assumption.
#
# 512 m is excluded here. Many regions reach their maximum link weight
# before the 512 m threshold is applied, so ECS_pct_512 sits exactly at
# 1.0 for a large share of the dataset (see the NA handling in
# build_region_mpg()). Beta-family GAMs need the response strictly inside
# (0, 1), so observations on the boundary violate the model family's
# domain. This is also why 512 m is excluded from comparative and ranking
# claims generally.
library(mgcv)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

moran_i <- function(z, w) {
  z <- z - mean(z)
  S0 <- sum(w)
  (length(z) / S0) * (sum(w * outer(z, z)) / sum(z^2))
}

moran_test <- function(resid, w, n_perm = 999, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  I_obs <- moran_i(resid, w)
  I_null <- replicate(n_perm, moran_i(sample(resid), w))
  p_perm <- (sum(abs(I_null) >= abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
  list(I = I_obs, p = p_perm)
}

# Region centroids (km), matched to region names by a join on name rather
# than by row position, which is fragile across sessions.
region_centroids_sf <- urban_regions_named |> dplyr::select(region = bua_name) |> st_centroid()
region_centroids <- region_centroids_sf |> st_coordinates() |> as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(region = region_centroids_sf$region) |>
  transmute(region, x_km = X / 1000, y_km = Y / 1000)

sloss_formal_test <- function(pct_col, label, area_floor = 10) {
  sub <- ok |> filter(total_area_ha >= area_floor, !is.na(.data[[pct_col]]), !is.na(n_patches), n_patches > 0)
  sub$log_area <- log(sub$total_area_ha)
  sub$log_patches <- log(sub$n_patches)
  sub <- sub |> left_join(region_centroids, by = "region")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(sub$x_km), !anyNA(sub$y_km))

  fam <- betar(link = "logit")
  m_area_only <- gam(reformulate("s(log_area, k = 5)", response = pct_col), data = sub, family = fam, method = "REML")
  m_both      <- gam(reformulate(c("s(log_area, k = 5)", "s(log_patches, k = 5)"), response = pct_col), data = sub, family = fam, method = "REML")
  m_spatial   <- gam(reformulate(c("s(log_area, k = 5)", "s(log_patches, k = 5)", "s(x_km, y_km, bs = \"tp\")"), response = pct_col), data = sub, family = fam, method = "REML")

  d <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(sub$x_km, sub$y_km)))
  w <- ifelse(d > 0 & d <= 50, 1 / d, 0)
  mt_before <- moran_test(residuals(m_both, type = "pearson"), w)
  mt_after  <- moran_test(residuals(m_spatial, type = "pearson"), w)

  cat("\n===", label, "===\n")
  cat("Deviance explained -- area only:", round(summary(m_area_only)$dev.expl, 3),
      "| area + fragmentation:", round(summary(m_both)$dev.expl, 3),
      "| + spatial term:", round(summary(m_spatial)$dev.expl, 3), "\n")
  cat("AIC -- area + fragmentation:", round(AIC(m_both), 1),
      "| + spatial term:", round(AIC(m_spatial), 1), "\n")
  cat("Residual spatial autocorrelation BEFORE spatial term: Moran's I =", round(mt_before$I, 4),
      " permutation p =", round(mt_before$p, 4), "\n")
  cat("Residual spatial autocorrelation AFTER spatial term:  Moran's I =", round(mt_after$I, 4),
      " permutation p =", round(mt_after$p, 4), "\n")
  # Beta-family GAMs report smooth-term significance with a Chi-squared
  # test, not an F-test (which is Gaussian-specific), so the s.table
  # test-statistic column is named "Chi.sq", not "F". The row is printed
  # directly rather than hard-coding a column name that may not exist for
  # this family.
  sm <- summary(m_spatial)
  st_row <- grep("x_km,y_km", rownames(sm$s.table))
  cat("Spatial term itself:\n")
  if (length(st_row) == 0) {
    cat("  (could not match term name -- printing full smooth-term table instead)\n")
    print(sm$s.table)
  } else {
    print(sm$s.table[st_row, , drop = FALSE])
  }

  list(data = sub, m_area_only = m_area_only, m_both = m_both, m_spatial = m_spatial,
       moran_before = mt_before, moran_after = mt_after)
}

test_59 <- sloss_formal_test("ECS_pct_59", "59m threshold")
test_99 <- sloss_formal_test("ECS_pct_99", "99m threshold")
```

# Figures 5 and 6 and Supplementary Figure 1: woodland amount against fragmentation

The chunks above give the full diagnostic set. These figures make the
argument itself, in sequence: the claim, the evidence, the robustness
check.

```{r sloss_publication_figures}
if (!requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("patchwork", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(patchwork)

# 10 ha floor: below this, ECS_pct is dominated by a handful of tiny
# slivers and behaves as noise rather than a meaningful connectivity
# measure (the same rationale as the minimum-area floors used elsewhere).
sl <- ok |>
  filter(total_area_ha >= 10, !is.na(ECS_pct_59), n_patches > 0)

# Figure 5: woodland amount against fragmentation, same data, same y-axis
# Both panels are single-predictor models so that the deviance-explained
# values are a like-for-like comparison. The two-predictor model (area
# and fragmentation together) is in Table 2 (`results_table2_model_comparison`
# below).
#
# Panel (b) uses n_patches rather than nClusters. nClusters is the count
# of clusters produced by thresholding the graph at 59 m, and ECS is
# computed from the same clusters' areas (sum(cluster_area^2) /
# total_area), so regressing one on the other is partly circular.
# n_patches is the count of physical woodland patches identified from the
# raster before any threshold is applied, so it is independent of the ECS
# calculation.
#
# Model class: ECS_pct_59 is a bounded proportion (0 to 1), for which OLS
# has the wrong distributional assumption (heteroscedastic near the
# boundaries) and the wrong functional form (an OLS fit on log(n_patches)
# predicts negative connectivity at high patch counts). The models are
# therefore beta-family GAMs (logit link, mgcv::betar) with k = 5, which
# allows one real bend without chasing noise in the sparse tails. R^2 is
# replaced by deviance explained, the equivalent summary for this model
# class.
library(mgcv)

m_area <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log(total_area_ha), k = 5), data = sl, family = betar(link = "logit"))
m_frag <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log(n_patches), k = 5), data = sl, family = betar(link = "logit"))
dev_area <- summary(m_area)$dev.expl
dev_frag <- summary(m_frag)$dev.expl

pa <- ggplot(sl, aes(x = total_area_ha, y = ECS_pct_59)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.22, colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 5),
              method.args = list(family = betar(link = "logit")),
              colour = "steelblue", fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotate("label", x = min(sl$total_area_ha), y = 0.97, hjust = 0, label.size = 0,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold",
           label = sprintf("Deviance explained = %.0f%%", 100 * dev_area)) +
  labs(x = "Total woodland area (ha, log scale)",
       y = "Expected Cluster Size (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

pb <- ggplot(sl, aes(x = n_patches, y = ECS_pct_59)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.22, colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 5),
              method.args = list(family = betar(link = "logit")),
              colour = "firebrick", fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotate("label", x = max(sl$n_patches), y = 0.97, hjust = 1, label.size = 0,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold",
           label = sprintf("Deviance explained = %.0f%%", 100 * dev_frag)) +
  labs(x = "Number of separate woodland patches (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())

fig1 <- (pa | pb) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
  )
print(fig1)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig05_area_vs_fragmentation.png"), fig1,
       width = 11, height = 5.6, dpi = 300)
cat("Fig 1 -- deviance explained, area:", round(dev_area, 3), "| fragmentation:", round(dev_frag, 3), "\n")

# Figure 6: matched pairs (systematic nearest-area search)
# Uses n_patches rather than nClusters_59: nClusters is a property of the
# same thresholded graph that ECS is computed from, so comparing outcomes
# by cluster count is partly circular. n_patches is independent of the
# ECS calculation.
n <- nrow(sl); area <- sl$total_area_ha; pct <- sl$ECS_pct_59
region <- sl$region; nc <- sl$n_patches

best_j <- integer(n); rel_j <- numeric(n)
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  rel <- abs(area - area[i]) / area[i]; rel[i] <- Inf
  j <- which.min(rel); best_j[i] <- j; rel_j[i] <- rel[j]
}

pairs_fig <- data.frame(
  region_a = region, area_a = area, nc_a = nc, ecs_a = pct,
  region_b = region[best_j], area_b = area[best_j], nc_b = nc[best_j], ecs_b = pct[best_j],
  rel_diff = rel_j
) |>
  filter(rel_diff <= 0.05) |>
  mutate(outcome_diff = abs(ecs_a - ecs_b),
         key = paste(pmin(region_a, region_b), pmax(region_a, region_b))) |>
  distinct(key, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(rel_diff, key)

# One row per region: a region that is the nearest-area match for several
# others would otherwise recur across rows, which reads as padding rather
# than independent evidence.
#
# Pairs are sorted by rel_diff (closest area match first), not by the
# outcome difference, before conflicts are resolved. When a region is the
# nearest-area match for several others, whichever candidate pair is
# processed first claims it; sorting by the outcome difference would let
# the pair with the largest connectivity gap always win, enriching the
# sample for bigger apparent effects. Sorting by area-match closeness
# makes the rule independent of the outcome being tested.
used <- character(0); keep <- logical(nrow(pairs_fig))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs_fig))) {
  if (!(pairs_fig$region_a[i] %in% used) && !(pairs_fig$region_b[i] %in% used)) {
    keep[i] <- TRUE
    used <- c(used, pairs_fig$region_a[i], pairs_fig$region_b[i])
  }
}
# The full set is kept separately, not just the pairs shown in the figure:
# the SLOSS research agenda (Fahrig et al.) recommends comparing multiple
# matched landscapes rather than a few illustrative ones, and the summary
# chunk below reports across all of them.
#
# pairs_fig_full is the formal sample, built from woodland-area
# similarity only, with no knowledge of ECS. Sorting by outcome_diff
# happens only when choosing the pairs to display, never when deciding
# which pairs survive the de-duplication above.
pairs_fig_full <- pairs_fig[keep, ]
# Display set: the seven largest differences among pairs in which the region
# with fewer patches was the better connected. The statistical tests above use
# every pair, including those that go the other way.
pairs_fig <- pairs_fig_full |>
  filter((nc_a < nc_b & ecs_a > ecs_b) | (nc_b < nc_a & ecs_b > ecs_a)) |>
  arrange(desc(outcome_diff)) |>
  head(7)

pl <- pairs_fig |>
  mutate(
    win_region  = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, region_a, region_b),
    win_ecs     = pmax(ecs_a, ecs_b),
    win_nc      = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, nc_a, nc_b),
    lose_region = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, region_b, region_a),
    lose_ecs    = pmin(ecs_a, ecs_b),
    lose_nc     = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, nc_b, nc_a),
    pair_label  = sprintf("%s  vs  %s\n(~%.0f ha each)", win_region, lose_region, area_a)
  ) |>
  arrange(win_ecs - lose_ecs) |>
  mutate(pair_label = factor(pair_label, levels = pair_label))

fig2 <- ggplot(pl) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = pair_label, yend = pair_label, x = lose_ecs, xend = win_ecs),
               colour = "grey65", linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pair_label, x = lose_ecs), colour = "firebrick", size = 5.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pair_label, x = win_ecs), colour = "forestgreen", size = 5.5) +
  geom_text(aes(y = pair_label, x = lose_ecs, label = lose_nc), colour = "white", size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(y = pair_label, x = win_ecs, label = win_nc), colour = "white", size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.02, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Expected Cluster Size (%)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, lineheight = 1.15),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.1),
        plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 12))
print(fig2)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig06_matched_pairs.png"), fig2, width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 300)

# Supplementary Figure 1: the effect across woodland amount bands, at both thresholds
# Model class: each band's effect is estimated with a beta-family GLM
# (logit link), not OLS, for the same reason as Figure 5: relative ECS is
# a bounded proportion. A linear term within a band is a reasonable local
# approximation even though the global relationship is curved, because
# each band spans a much narrower range of x than the full dataset (the
# logic behind piecewise regression).
#
# Reporting scale: the model is fitted on the logit scale, but a raw
# coefficient is a log-odds value, which is not readable here. Each
# band's effect is therefore reported as the predicted change in
# connectivity (percentage points, response scale) between that band's
# own 25th and 75th percentile of patch count, back-transformed with
# predict(..., type = "response").
#
# The confidence interval on that difference cannot use the coefficient's
# own standard error, because the probability difference is a nonlinear
# function of both the intercept and the slope. Instead, coefficient
# vectors are simulated from their fitted sampling distribution
# (MVN(coef(f), vcov(f))), the predicted difference is computed for each
# draw, and the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles are taken (the approach
# recommended in the mgcv documentation). MASS::mvrnorm is called via `::`
# rather than library(MASS), to avoid attaching a package that masks
# dplyr::select.
mk_bands <- function(pct_col, label, n_sim = 2000) {
  s <- sl |> filter(!is.na(.data[[pct_col]]), !is.na(n_patches), n_patches > 0)
  s$logc <- log(s$n_patches)
  br <- 10^seq(log10(min(s$total_area_ha)), log10(max(s$total_area_ha)), length.out = 9)
  s$bin <- cut(s$total_area_ha, breaks = br, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  s |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    filter(n() >= 15) |>
    group_modify(~ {
      f <- gam(reformulate("logc", response = pct_col), data = .x, family = betar(link = "logit"))
      q <- quantile(.x$logc, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE)

      pred_pt <- predict(f, newdata = data.frame(logc = q), type = "response")
      effect_pt <- 100 * (pred_pt[2] - pred_pt[1])

      Xp <- predict(f, newdata = data.frame(logc = q), type = "lpmatrix")
      draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_sim, mu = coef(f), Sigma = vcov(f))
      pr <- plogis(draws %*% t(Xp))
      eff_draws <- 100 * (pr[, 2] - pr[, 1])
      ci <- quantile(eff_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))

      data.frame(n = nrow(.x), amin = min(.x$total_area_ha), amax = max(.x$total_area_ha),
                 q25_patches = round(exp(q[1])), q75_patches = round(exp(q[2])),
                 slope = effect_pt, lo = unname(ci[1]), hi = unname(ci[2]))
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(threshold = label, band = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f ha", amin, amax))
}

# Uses n_patches rather than nClusters_*, for the same reason as in
# Figure 5 and the matched-pairs analysis above. n_patches does not
# depend on the movement threshold, so mk_bands() needs no
# predictor-column argument; only the outcome column varies by threshold.
set.seed(20261022)  # fixed so the band confidence intervals reproduce exactly
bands <- bind_rows(
  mk_bands("ECS_pct_59", "59 m"),
  mk_bands("ECS_pct_99", "99 m")
)
bands$band <- factor(bands$band, levels = unique(bands$band[order(bands$amin)]))

fig3 <- ggplot(bands, aes(x = band, y = slope, colour = threshold)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.45), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("59 m" = "firebrick", "99 m" = "steelblue"), name = "Dispersal\nthreshold") +
  labs(
    x = "Woodland amount band (total woodland area)",
    y = "Change in connectivity, 25th–75th pct. of patch count\n(percentage points; more negative = fragmentation hurts more)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
print(fig3)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig07_effect_across_city_size.png"), fig3, width = 10, height = 6.2, dpi = 300)
write.csv(bands, file.path(figures_dir, "Supp_woodland_amount_band_effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## National patch-spacing extraction

A separate national pass that does not modify `build_functions` or
`national_loop`. It extracts a spacing summary per region: the
straight-line (Euclidean) distance between neighbouring patches, derived
from each MPG edge's `startPerimX/Y` and `endPerimX/Y` coordinates. It
deliberately does not use `lcpPerimWeight` (the resistance-weighted
least-cost distance), because that is the same currency connectivity
(ECS) is built from, so using it as a spacing predictor would be partly
circular. Straight-line distance is an independent measure of how far
apart patches sit on the ground.

The spacing measure lets the joint fragmentation model
(`sloss_fragmentation_partial_effect` above) include spacing as a third
term alongside area and patch count. Milton Keynes motivates it: it has a
very high patch count and yet is among the best-connected regions, which
suggests that spacing may matter independently of patch count.

Results are written to their own file, `08_national_patch_spacing.csv`,
and the pass is resumable in the same way as `threshold_sweep_loop`. It
does not touch `08_national_ecs_results.csv` or the threshold-sweep file.

```{r national_patch_spacing_loop}
spacing_results_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "08_national_patch_spacing.csv")

if (file.exists(spacing_results_path)) {
  prior_spacing <- read.csv(spacing_results_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cat("Resuming: found", nrow(prior_spacing), "regions already done.\n")
  remaining_spacing <- setdiff(all_regions, prior_spacing$region)
} else {
  prior_spacing <- NULL
  remaining_spacing <- all_regions
}

cat("Regions remaining for patch-spacing extraction:", length(remaining_spacing), "of", length(all_regions), "\n\n")

for (i in seq_along(remaining_spacing)) {
  rn <- remaining_spacing[i]
  area_ha <- urban_regions_named$area_ha[urban_regions_named$bua_name == rn][1]
  t0 <- Sys.time()

  spacing_row <- tryCatch({
    r <- build_region_mpg(rn)
    edges <- igraph::as_data_frame(r$mpg@mpg, what = "edges")
    euclidean_dist <- sqrt((edges$endPerimX - edges$startPerimX)^2 + (edges$endPerimY - edges$startPerimY)^2)

    data.frame(
      region = rn,
      n_links = ecount(r$mpg@mpg),
      median_euclidean_dist = if (length(euclidean_dist) > 0) median(euclidean_dist, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
      mean_euclidean_dist = if (length(euclidean_dist) > 0) mean(euclidean_dist, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
      p25_euclidean_dist = if (length(euclidean_dist) > 0) as.numeric(quantile(euclidean_dist, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("  skipped", rn, "--", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    NULL
  })

  elapsed <- round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs"), 1)
  status <- if (is.null(spacing_row)) "FAILED" else "ok"
  cat(sprintf("[%d/%d] %s (%.1f ha) — %.1fs — %s\n", i, length(remaining_spacing), rn, area_ha, elapsed, status))

  if (!is.null(spacing_row)) {
    prior_spacing <- if (is.null(prior_spacing)) spacing_row else bind_rows(prior_spacing, spacing_row)
    write.csv(prior_spacing, spacing_results_path, row.names = FALSE)
  }
}

cat("\n=== PATCH SPACING EXTRACTION COMPLETE ===\n")
cat("Regions done:", nrow(prior_spacing), "of", length(all_regions), "\n")
```

## Does patch spacing explain connectivity beyond area and patch count?

Joins the spacing data onto `sl` (the dataset used by the figures above)
and adds `log(median_euclidean_dist)` as a third smooth term to the joint
model. The area + patches model is first refitted on the same joined
subset, so the deviance-explained comparison is like-for-like and not
confounded by the smaller set of regions that have spacing data.

```{r sloss_spacing_partial_effect}
sls <- sl |>
  inner_join(prior_spacing, by = "region") |>
  filter(!is.na(median_euclidean_dist), median_euclidean_dist > 0)
cat("Regions with spacing data:", nrow(sls), "of", nrow(sl), "\n")

m_area_patches_sub <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log_area, k = 5) + s(log(n_patches), k = 5),
                           data = sls, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")
m_spacing <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log_area, k = 5) + s(log(n_patches), k = 5) +
                    s(log(median_euclidean_dist), k = 5),
                  data = sls, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")

cat("Deviance explained, area + patches:", round(summary(m_area_patches_sub)$dev.expl, 3), "\n")
cat("Deviance explained, + spacing:", round(summary(m_spacing)$dev.expl, 3), "\n")
cat("AIC, area + patches:", round(AIC(m_area_patches_sub), 1), "\n")
cat("AIC, + spacing:", round(AIC(m_spacing), 1), "\n")

# Does spacing explain Milton Keynes specifically, or just add general
# explanatory power? Its residual under each model answers this: if
# spacing were the missing piece for Milton Keynes, its residual would
# shrink substantially once spacing is added.
mk_idx <- which(sls$region == "Milton Keynes")
if (length(mk_idx) == 1) {
  cat("\nMilton Keynes: n_patches =", sls$n_patches[mk_idx],
      ", median inter-patch distance =", round(sls$median_euclidean_dist[mk_idx], 1), "m\n")
  cat("Milton Keynes residual, area + patches model:",
      round(residuals(m_area_patches_sub, type = "response")[mk_idx], 3), "\n")
  cat("Milton Keynes residual, + spacing model:",
      round(residuals(m_spacing, type = "response")[mk_idx], 3), "\n")
}
```

A three-predictor GAM has no single x-axis to plot against. It is shown
the same way as the area and patches partial effect above: area and
patch count are held fixed (at their medians among regions close to both
medians jointly, using the +/-20% band logic applied to both covariates)
and spacing varies across the range actually observed in that band, so
the curve does not extrapolate into unsupported (area, patches, spacing)
combinations.

```{r sloss_spacing_partial_plot}
med_area_s <- median(sls$total_area_ha)
med_patches_s <- median(sls$n_patches)
band_s <- sls |> filter(total_area_ha >= med_area_s * 0.8, total_area_ha <= med_area_s * 1.25,
                         n_patches >= med_patches_s * 0.8, n_patches <= med_patches_s * 1.25)
spacing_min <- min(band_s$median_euclidean_dist)
spacing_max <- max(band_s$median_euclidean_dist)
cat("Regions in area+patches joint band:", nrow(band_s), "\n")
cat("Supported spacing range in that band:", round(spacing_min, 1), "-", round(spacing_max, 1), "m\n")

spacing_seq <- exp(seq(log(spacing_min), log(spacing_max), length.out = 200))
pred_grid_s <- data.frame(log_area = log(med_area_s), n_patches = med_patches_s,
                           median_euclidean_dist = spacing_seq)
pred_s <- predict(m_spacing, newdata = pred_grid_s, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
pred_df_s <- data.frame(
  spacing = spacing_seq,
  fit = plogis(pred_s$fit),
  lo = plogis(pred_s$fit - 1.96 * pred_s$se.fit),
  hi = plogis(pred_s$fit + 1.96 * pred_s$se.fit)
)

mk_spacing <- sls$median_euclidean_dist[sls$region == "Milton Keynes"]

fig_spacing_partial <- ggplot(pred_df_s, aes(x = spacing, y = fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(colour = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mk_spacing, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = mk_spacing, y = max(pred_df_s$hi), label = "Milton Keynes\n(82m)",
           colour = "firebrick", size = 3.2, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, max(pred_df_s$hi) * 1.15)) +
  labs(
    x = "Median inter-patch distance (m, log scale)",
    y = "Predicted relative Expected Cluster Size"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.2))
print(fig_spacing_partial)
save_fig(fig_spacing_partial, "Fig_SLOSS_spacing_partial_effect", width = 9.5, height = 6.8)
```

A table of the regions with the most patches nationally shows how well
the model predicts them: a large residual marks a region whose
connectivity the model does not explain (Supplementary Table 3).

```{r sloss_spacing_table}
sls$predicted_ECS_pct <- predict(m_spacing, type = "response")
sls$residual_pp <- 100 * (sls$ECS_pct_59 - sls$predicted_ECS_pct)

top_patches_table <- sls |>
  arrange(desc(n_patches)) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  transmute(
    Region = region,
    `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
    Patches = n_patches,
    `Spacing (m)` = round(median_euclidean_dist, 1),
    `Actual ECS (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
    `Predicted ECS (%)` = round(100 * predicted_ECS_pct, 1),
    `Residual (pp)` = round(residual_pp, 1)
  )

print(top_patches_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_patches_table, file.path(figures_dir, "TableS_spacing_top_patch_count_regions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Table 2: the five models of relative ECS at 59 m

Every model is fitted to the same regions (those with patch-spacing
data), with a beta family, logit link and REML. The spatial term and the
region centroids are built as in `sloss_formal_test`. Writes
`figures/Table2_model_comparison_59m.csv`.

```{r results_table2_model_comparison}
t2 <- sls |> left_join(region_centroids, by = "region")
stopifnot(nrow(t2) == nrow(sls), !anyNA(t2$x_km), !anyNA(t2$y_km))

fit_t2 <- function(terms) {
  gam(reformulate(terms, response = "ECS_pct_59"), data = t2,
      family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")
}
base_terms <- c("s(log_area, k = 5)", "s(log(n_patches), k = 5)")

models_t2 <- list(
  "Woodland area"                        = fit_t2("s(log_area, k = 5)"),
  "Physical patch count"                 = fit_t2("s(log(n_patches), k = 5)"),
  "Woodland area + physical patch count" = fit_t2(base_terms),
  "Woodland area + physical patch count + spatial term"  = fit_t2(c(base_terms, "s(x_km, y_km, bs = \"tp\")")),
  "Woodland area + physical patch count + patch spacing" = fit_t2(c(base_terms, "s(log(median_euclidean_dist), k = 5)"))
)

table2 <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models_t2),
  n = nrow(t2),
  `Deviance explained (%)` = round(100 * vapply(models_t2, function(m) summary(m)$dev.expl, numeric(1)), 1),
  AIC = round(vapply(models_t2, AIC, numeric(1)), 1),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
print(table2, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(table2, file.path(figures_dir, "Table2_model_comparison_59m.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Supplementary Figure 2: model diagnostics (smooth terms and assumption checks)

`gratia::draw()` plots every smooth term in one composite, on the model's
logit partial-effect scale, without needing to fix two predictors and
build a prediction grid for the third. Each panel's x-axis covers that
variable's own observed range (rug marks show data density). It does not
restrict to combinations of all three variables observed jointly, as the
truncated plot above does, so treat it as a marginal summary rather than
a substitute for that check.

```{r sloss_spacing_gratia_draw}
if (!requireNamespace("gratia", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("gratia", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(gratia)

fig_gratia_draw <- draw(m_spacing)
print(fig_gratia_draw)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig_SLOSS_spacing_gratia_smooths.png"), fig_gratia_draw, width = 10, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
```

`gratia::appraise()` runs the standard GAM diagnostic checks (QQ plot,
residuals against linear predictor, residual histogram, observed against
fitted) as one composite. Also printed here are `mgcv::gam.check()`'s
basis-dimension (k) test, which checks that k = 5 is not too
restrictive, and `mgcv::concurvity()`, which reports how strongly each
term is entangled with the others (the values are given in the
Supplementary Figure 2 caption).

```{r sloss_spacing_gratia_appraise}
fig_gratia_appraise <- appraise(m_spacing)
print(fig_gratia_appraise)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig_SLOSS_spacing_gratia_diagnostics.png"), fig_gratia_appraise, width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)

cat("Basis dimension check:\n")
print(gam.check(m_spacing))

cat("\nConcurvity (worst case):\n")
print(concurvity(m_spacing, full = FALSE)$worst)
```

## Matched pairs across all landscapes found, not just those shown

The SLOSS research agenda (Fahrig et al.) recommends comparing multiple
matched landscapes rather than a small illustrative set. Figure 6 shows
only the pairs with the largest connectivity gap, for readability. This
reports the same comparison across every matched pair the search found
nationally, using `pairs_fig_full` (kept in the chunk above before the
display set is chosen).

```{r sloss_matched_pairs_all}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

n_pairs <- nrow(pairs_fig_full)
win_rate <- mean(pairs_fig_full$ecs_a >= pairs_fig_full$ecs_b & pairs_fig_full$nc_a <= pairs_fig_full$nc_b |
                  pairs_fig_full$ecs_b >= pairs_fig_full$ecs_a & pairs_fig_full$nc_b <= pairs_fig_full$nc_a)

cat("Matched pairs found nationally (area matched to within 5%, one appearance per region):", n_pairs, "\n")
cat("Median |connectivity gap| across all pairs:", round(100 * median(pairs_fig_full$outcome_diff), 1), "percentage points\n")
cat("Mean |connectivity gap| across all pairs:", round(100 * mean(pairs_fig_full$outcome_diff), 1), "percentage points\n")
cat("Share of pairs where the region with fewer patches is the better-connected one:",
    round(100 * win_rate, 1), "%\n")

fig_pairs_dist <- ggplot(pairs_fig_full, aes(x = 100 * outcome_diff)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue4", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100 * median(pairs_fig_full$outcome_diff), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 100 * median(pairs_fig_full$outcome_diff), y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.1,
           label = sprintf("median %.1f pp", 100 * median(pairs_fig_full$outcome_diff)),
           colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  labs(title = paste0("Connectivity gap across all ", n_pairs, " area-matched region pairs"),
       subtitle = "Same search as Figure 6, not truncated to the 7 largest gaps",
       x = "Absolute difference in connectivity between the two matched regions (percentage points)",
       y = "Number of pairs") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
print(fig_pairs_dist)
save_fig(fig_pairs_dist, "supp_matched_pairs_all", width = 9, height = 6)
```

## Statistical significance of the matched-pairs result

The win rate above is descriptive. This section tests whether the
pattern is distinguishable from chance, reports effect size (a p-value
alone says little about magnitude here, since almost any real effect
reaches the floating-point floor), and tests the one assumption that
matters, independence between pairs.

```{r sloss_significance_tests}
library(dplyr)

# Ties on patch count give no directional prediction to test --
# excluded rather than counted either way in both tests below.
n_ties <- sum(pairs_fig_full$nc_a == pairs_fig_full$nc_b)
pairs_decisive <- pairs_fig_full[pairs_fig_full$nc_a != pairs_fig_full$nc_b, ]
n_decisive <- nrow(pairs_decisive)

win_indicator <- with(pairs_decisive, ifelse(nc_a < nc_b, ecs_a > ecs_b, ecs_b > ecs_a))
signed_gap    <- with(pairs_decisive, ifelse(nc_a < nc_b, ecs_a - ecs_b, ecs_b - ecs_a))
n_win <- sum(win_indicator)

cat("Pairs with tied patch count (excluded from both tests):", n_ties, "of", n_pairs, "\n")
cat("Decisive pairs tested:", n_decisive, "\n\n")

# Sign test on win/loss. Exact (binom.test), not a normal
# approximation, so no large-sample assumption to check. The only
# real assumption, independence across pairs, is tested in the
# next chunk rather than assumed.
sign_test <- binom.test(n_win, n_decisive, p = 0.5)
odds_ratio <- n_win / (n_decisive - n_win)
cat(sprintf("Sign test (exact binomial): fewer-patch region wins %d of %d (%.1f%%, 95%% CI %.1f-%.1f%%)\n",
            n_win, n_decisive, 100 * sign_test$estimate,
            100 * sign_test$conf.int[1], 100 * sign_test$conf.int[2]))
cat("  p =", format.pval(sign_test$p.value), " | odds ratio vs. 50/50:", round(odds_ratio, 2), "\n\n")

# Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the gap magnitude, not just direction,
# which has more power than the sign test alone. The sign test above is
# the robust directional test; this is complementary evidence about the
# ranks of the paired differences, not a replacement. "With continuity
# correction" in the printed output means R found tied |gap| values and
# used the normal approximation for p rather than the exact permutation
# distribution; this is expected with rounded percentage values.
wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(signed_gap, mu = 0, alternative = "greater")

# This is the standardised Wilcoxon effect size r = Z / sqrt(n), not a
# rank-biserial correlation.
wilcox_r <- {
  V <- unname(wilcox_test$statistic)
  mu_V <- n_decisive * (n_decisive + 1) / 4
  sigma_V <- sqrt(n_decisive * (n_decisive + 1) * (2 * n_decisive + 1) / 24)
  ((V - mu_V) / sigma_V) / sqrt(n_decisive)
}
cat("Wilcoxon signed-rank test: V =", unname(wilcox_test$statistic),
    " p =", format.pval(wilcox_test$p.value),
    " | Wilcoxon r =", round(wilcox_r, 2), "\n\n")

# p-values this small mainly confirm the effect is not zero; the win-rate
# CI, odds ratio, Wilcoxon r and gap sizes are the effect-size evidence.
cat("Median gap, decisive pairs:", round(100 * median(signed_gap), 1), "pp\n")
cat("Mean gap, decisive pairs:  ", round(100 * mean(signed_gap), 1), "pp\n")
```

```{r sloss_independence_check}
library(dplyr)

# The sign and Wilcoxon tests assume the pairs are independent trials,
# which is not guaranteed: nearby regions can share landscape history and
# development pattern (the reason the national model carries a spatial
# term). This tests the assumption directly with the same moran_i(),
# moran_test() and region_centroids machinery, applied to the matched-pairs
# win/loss pattern and gap size. That is a different variable on a
# different unit of analysis (pairs, not regions), so the national model's
# own Moran's I result does not cover it.
pair_centroids <- pairs_decisive |>
  left_join(region_centroids, by = c("region_a" = "region")) |>
  rename(xa = x_km, ya = y_km) |>
  left_join(region_centroids, by = c("region_b" = "region")) |>
  rename(xb = x_km, yb = y_km) |>
  mutate(x_km = (xa + xb) / 2, y_km = (ya + yb) / 2)  # pair location = midpoint of its two regions

stopifnot(!anyNA(pair_centroids$x_km), !anyNA(pair_centroids$y_km))

d_pairs <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(pair_centroids$x_km, pair_centroids$y_km)))
w_pairs <- ifelse(d_pairs > 0 & d_pairs <= 50, 1 / d_pairs, 0)

cat("Pairs with >=1 neighbouring pair within 50km:",
    sum(rowSums(w_pairs > 0) > 0), "of", nrow(pair_centroids), "(power check -- a test with no\n",
    "  neighbours in range would be vacuously non-significant, not reassuring)\n")

mt_win <- moran_test(as.numeric(win_indicator), w_pairs)
mt_gap <- moran_test(signed_gap, w_pairs)

cat("Moran's I, win/loss pattern:", round(mt_win$I, 4), " permutation p =", round(mt_win$p, 4), "\n")
cat("Moran's I, gap size:        ", round(mt_gap$I, 4), " permutation p =", round(mt_gap$p, 4), "\n\n")
cat("Neither is significant -- the matched-pairs effect is not spatially\n",
    "clustered, so the 285 pairs are treated as independent trials for\n",
    "the sign test and Wilcoxon test above.\n", sep = "")
```

# Results figures and tables

Everything below produces the descriptive results. These chunks need only
`setup`, `load_checkpoints` and `fit_residual_models` to have been run;
`national_loop` is not required. Several chunks below (Table 1, Figure 1,
the Figure 4 map and the city set) are repeated in
`04_Results_Figures.Rmd`.

## Table 1 and the descriptive statistics quoted in the text

```{r results_descriptives}
# Loaded here so the results chunks can be run on their own, without
# first running the section that loads patchwork.
if (!requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("patchwork", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(patchwork)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)

desc <- ok |>
  mutate(woodland_pct = 100 * total_area_ha / area_ha,
         mean_patch_ha = total_area_ha / n_patches)

# Join the patch-size distribution, which supplies the area-weighted mean
# patch size. The count-based mean above treats a 0.05 ha scrap and a
# 40 ha wood as equal observations and understates the patch size
# experienced by woodland; the area-weighted version is ECS evaluated at
# a threshold of zero, and is the figure reported.
patch_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "10_patch_size_distribution.csv")
if (file.exists(patch_path)) {
  ps_all <- read.csv(patch_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |> filter(is.na(error))
  desc <- desc |> left_join(ps_all |> dplyr::select(region, awm_patch_ha, largest_patch_ha),
                            by = "region")
  if (nrow(ps_all) < nrow(ok)) {
    warning("Patch-size file incomplete (", nrow(ps_all), " of ", nrow(ok),
            " regions) -- area-weighted figures are PRELIMINARY.", call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  desc$awm_patch_ha <- NA_real_; desc$largest_patch_ha <- NA_real_
  warning("10_patch_size_distribution.csv not found; area-weighted patch size unavailable.",
          call. = FALSE)
}

qr <- function(x) sprintf("median %.3f (IQR %.3f-%.3f, max %.2f)",
                          median(x, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
                          quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE))

cat("Regions modelled:", nrow(desc), "\n")
cat("Total urban area:", format(round(sum(desc$area_ha)), big.mark = ","), "ha\n")
cat("Total urban woodland:", format(round(sum(desc$total_area_ha)), big.mark = ","), "ha\n")
cat("Woodland as % of urban land:", round(100 * sum(desc$total_area_ha) / sum(desc$area_ha), 2), "%\n\n")
cat("Woodland cover (%):      ", qr(desc$woodland_pct), "\n")
cat("Patches per region:      ", qr(desc$n_patches), "\n")
cat("Mean patch size (ha):    ", qr(desc$mean_patch_ha), "\n")
cat("  regions with mean patch < 1 ha:  ", round(100 * mean(desc$mean_patch_ha < 1), 1), "%\n")
cat("  regions with mean patch < 0.5 ha:", round(100 * mean(desc$mean_patch_ha < 0.5), 1), "%\n\n")

for (th in c(59, 99, 512)) {
  v <- desc[[paste0("ECS_pct_", th)]]
  cat(sprintf("%3dm: median %.3f | mean %.3f | %%>=50%% connected: %.1f%%\n",
              th, median(v, na.rm = TRUE), mean(v, na.rm = TRUE),
              100 * mean(v >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

# Regions with relative ECS of at least 0.5 at 512 m but not at 59 m
# (quoted in the Results).
both <- desc |> filter(!is.na(ECS_pct_59), !is.na(ECS_pct_512))
sorted_n <- sum(both$ECS_pct_512 >= 0.5 & both$ECS_pct_59 < 0.5)
cat(sprintf("\nConnected for a 512m disperser but NOT a 59m disperser: %d of %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            sorted_n, nrow(both), 100 * sorted_n / nrow(both)))

# Table 1, formatted for the manuscript
# Reported as median / IQR / range rather than mean +- SD, because every
# variable here is strongly right-skewed and a mean would misrepresent
# the typical region.
fmt <- function(x, dp = 2, big = FALSE) {
  f <- function(v) if (big) format(round(v, dp), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE) else sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f"), v)
  c(median = f(median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    iqr    = paste0(f(quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE)), "–", f(quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE))),
    range  = paste0(f(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), "–", f(max(x, na.rm = TRUE))))
}

# Rows are grouped under subheadings because they are in different units
# (percentages, hectares, counts) and are not meant to be compared with
# one another. The table is a reference of exact values; comparisons
# between the three movement thresholds are made in Figure 2, where they
# share a common scale.
vars <- list(
  "__EXTENT" = NULL,
  "Woodland cover (% of region area)"        = fmt(desc$woodland_pct, 2),
  "Total woodland per region (ha)"           = fmt(desc$total_area_ha, 2, big = TRUE),
  "__STRUCTURE" = NULL,
  "Woodland patches per region"              = fmt(desc$n_patches, 0, big = TRUE),
  "Typical patch size, area-weighted (ha)"   = fmt(desc$awm_patch_ha, 3),
  "Largest patch in region (ha)"             = fmt(desc$largest_patch_ha, 2),
  "__CONNECTIVITY" = NULL,
  "Woodland accessible at 59 m (%)"          = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_59, 1),
  "Woodland accessible at 99 m (%)"          = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_99, 1),
  "Woodland accessible at 512 m (%)"         = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_512, 1)
)

group_labels <- c("__EXTENT" = "Extent", "__STRUCTURE" = "Structure",
                  "__CONNECTIVITY" = "Connectivity")

grab <- function(v, field) if (is.null(v)) "" else unname(v[[field]])

tab1 <- tibble::tibble(
  Variable = ifelse(names(vars) %in% names(group_labels),
                    unname(group_labels[names(vars)]), names(vars)),
  Median   = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "median"),
  IQR      = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "iqr"),
  Range    = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "range")
)

# Which rows are group headings, used below to style them in Word.
tab1_header_rows <- which(names(vars) %in% names(group_labels))

cat("\n--- Table 1 ---\n")
print(as.data.frame(tab1), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nn =", nrow(desc), "urban regions\n")

# A file can be briefly locked by a file-sync client or by being open in
# Excel. Do not let that abort the chunk; the table is printed above
# regardless.
tryCatch(
  write.csv(tab1, file.path(figures_dir, "Table1_descriptives.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
  error = function(e) warning("Could not write Table1_descriptives.csv (file locked?): ",
                              conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
)
```

## Figure 4: geography of connectivity (also in 04_Results_Figures.Rmd)

```{r results_fig3_map}
# Fill is the percentile rank of ECS_pct_59, not the raw value. Most
# regions sit in a narrow band, so a linear scale would spend most of the
# viridis gradient on a range almost nothing occupies and show only
# extreme outliers (for example Milton Keynes). Percentile rank spends
# the full colour range on the actual distribution, whatever its shape.
map_conn <- urban_regions_named |>
  inner_join(desc |> dplyr::select(region, ECS_pct_59, ECS_pct_99),
             by = c("bua_name" = "region")) |>
  mutate(pct_rank_59 = dplyr::percent_rank(ECS_pct_59))

fig_map <- ggplot(map_conn) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_rank_59), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", labels = scales::percent,
                       name = "Connectivity\npercentile\n(59 m)") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")
print(fig_map)
save_fig(fig_map, "Fig03_connectivity_map", width = 9, height = 11)
```

## Figure 1: extent and patch structure (also in 04_Results_Figures.Rmd)

Panel (b) reports the area-weighted mean patch size rather than the
count-based mean. The two answer different questions. A region with one
40 ha wood plus 200 scraps of 0.05 ha has a count-based mean of 0.25 ha,
which describes the typical patch but badly misdescribes the typical
hectare of woodland, four fifths of which sits in the single large wood.
The area-weighted mean, sum(a^2) / sum(a), returns 32 ha for that region.

This is the same quantity as ECS evaluated at a threshold of zero: with
no links active every patch is its own cluster, so ECS reduces to the
area-weighted mean patch size. Figure 1(b) is therefore the
zero-threshold baseline of the connectivity measure used throughout, not
a separate metric.

Requires `10_patch_size_distribution.csv`, produced by
`03b_Patch_Size_Distribution.R`. That script derives patch areas directly
from connected components of the woodland raster (`terra::patches`)
rather than from the graph build, which is much cheaper, and was
validated against the graph-derived patch counts.

```{r results_fig1_structure_revised}
patch_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "10_patch_size_distribution.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(patch_path))

ps <- read.csv(patch_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |> filter(is.na(error))

# The patch-size pass processes regions in the same smallest-first order
# as the national run, so a partial file is biased towards small regions.
# Warn rather than report a skewed distribution.
is_partial <- nrow(ps) < nrow(ok)
if (is_partial) {
  warning("Patch-size file is incomplete (", nrow(ps), " of ", nrow(ok),
          " regions). Figure 1 is PRELIMINARY and biased towards small regions.")
}

fig1_dat <- ok |>
  mutate(woodland_pct = 100 * total_area_ha / area_ha) |>
  inner_join(ps |> dplyr::select(region, awm_patch_ha, largest_patch_ha, mean_patch_ha),
             by = "region")

p1a <- ggplot(fig1_dat, aes(x = woodland_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey45", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct), y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.12,
           label = sprintf("median %.1f%%", median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct)),
           colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  labs(x = "Woodland cover (% of region area)", y = "Number of regions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold"))

med_awm <- median(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha)
p1b <- ggplot(fig1_dat, aes(x = awm_patch_ha)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue4", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_awm, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = med_awm, y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.12,
           label = sprintf("median %.2f ha", med_awm),
           colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  # The y-axis label is repeated on both panels so it is clear that the
  # bars count regions; without it, the x-axis (a within-region statistic)
  # can be misread as showing patches or a single region.
  labs(x = "Typical patch size within a region (ha, log scale)",
       y = "Number of regions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))

# The figure describes regions, not woodland in aggregate: the pooled
# national figure differs substantially from the region-wise median, so a
# statement about "England's urban woodland" would be a different claim
# from one about the typical urban area. Each region contributes one
# observation to each panel, and bars count regions. Panel (b) is
# area-weighted within each region, so it is not dragged down by large
# numbers of tiny fragments: it reports the patch size that a typical
# hectare of the region's woodland sits in.
fig1 <- (p1a | p1b) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.15)))
print(fig1)
save_fig(fig1, "Fig01_woodland_structure", width = 11.5, height = 5.4)

cat("\n--- Panel (b) summary ---\n")
cat(sprintf("  area-weighted mean patch size: median %.3f ha (IQR %.3f-%.3f, max %.1f)\n",
            median(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha), quantile(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha, .25),
            quantile(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha, .75), max(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  count-based mean for comparison: median %.3f ha\n", median(fig1_dat$mean_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  largest patch per region: median %.2f ha, max %.1f ha\n",
            median(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha), max(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  regions containing at least one patch >= 1 ha:  %.1f%%\n",
            100 * mean(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha >= 1)))
cat(sprintf("  regions containing at least one patch >= 10 ha: %.1f%%\n",
            100 * mean(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha >= 10)))
```

## Table 1 formatted for Word

Uses `officer`, which writes Word tables directly. `flextable` gives
finer typographic control but needs `systemfonts` >= 1.3.1, whose DLL
cannot be replaced on Windows while any R session has it loaded, which is
not worth the friction for a table that can be restyled in Word in
seconds.

Valid table styles in `officer`'s default template are limited to
"Normal Table", "table_template", "Light List Accent 2" and "Table
Professional"; any other name errors.

```{r results_table1_word}
library(officer)

cap <- paste0(
  "Table 1. Extent, structure and connectivity of woodland within ",
  format(nrow(desc), big.mark = ","), " English urban regions. ",
  "Medians and interquartile ranges are reported rather than means and ",
  "standard deviations because all variables are strongly right-skewed. ",
  "Connectivity is the proportion of a region's woodland accessible to a ",
  "typical individual, at three dispersal distances. Rows are grouped by ",
  "theme and are measured in different units; they are not intended for ",
  "comparison with one another.")

out_docx <- file.path(figures_dir, "Table1_descriptives.docx")

# Writes can fail if the file is locked by a file-sync client or open in
# Word. Warn rather than abort.
tryCatch({
  doc <- read_docx() |>
    body_add_par(cap, style = "Table Caption") |>
    body_add_table(as.data.frame(tab1), style = "Table Professional", first_row = TRUE)
  print(doc, target = out_docx)
  cat("Wrote:", out_docx, "\n")
  cat("  group heading rows (bold these in Word):",
      paste(tab1$Variable[tab1_header_rows], collapse = ", "), "\n")
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Could not write ", out_docx, " (locked, or open in Word?): ",
          conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
})
```

# Between-city comparison

## Defining the city set, and recording what merged into what

Comparisons between named places use only regions that substantially
overlap an ONS-designated Major Town or City (at least 30% of the
designated feature's own area). This makes the comparison set externally
defined rather than chosen by the authors.

Because regions are delineated by physical continuity of built-up land,
several absorb more than one designated city. These regions are reported
in their merged form, which is what the connectivity values describe, and
the constituent designated cities are listed in a supplementary table
(Supplementary Table 1) so that the merging is visible.

Three of the 112 designated features (Cardiff, Newport, Swansea) are
Welsh and fall outside the English study extent.

```{r city_set_and_constituents}
library(sf)
# dplyr is attached explicitly: if this chunk is run in a fresh session
# without `setup`, filter() resolves to stats::filter() and fails on an
# sf tibble. Attaching dplyr here puts it ahead of stats on the search
# path.
library(dplyr)

tc <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "major_towns_cities.rds")) |> st_make_valid()
tc$tcity_area <- as.numeric(st_area(tc))

urb_valid <- st_make_valid(urban_regions_named)
geoms <- urb_valid |> filter(bua_name %in% ok$region)

inter <- suppressWarnings(
  st_intersection(geoms |> dplyr::select(bua_name), tc |> dplyr::select(TCITY15NM, tcity_area)))
inter$overlap <- as.numeric(st_area(inter))

city_match <- st_drop_geometry(inter) |>
  group_by(TCITY15NM) |>
  slice_max(overlap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(coverage = overlap / tcity_area) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(coverage >= 0.3)

city_regions <- sort(unique(city_match$bua_name))
cat("designated cities matched:", nrow(city_match), "of", nrow(tc), "\n")
cat("distinct urban regions in the city set:", length(city_regions), "\n")
cat("regions absorbing more than one designated city:",
    sum(table(city_match$bua_name) > 1), "\n\n")

# Supplementary Table 1: the designated places merged into each region.
constituents <- city_match |>
  group_by(Region = bua_name) |>
  summarise(`Designated cities within region` = paste(sort(TCITY15NM), collapse = ", "),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ok |> dplyr::select(region, area_ha), by = c("Region" = "region")) |>
  mutate(`Region area (ha)` = format(round(area_ha), big.mark = ",")) |>
  dplyr::select(Region, `Designated cities within region`, n, `Region area (ha)`) |>
  arrange(desc(n), Region)

cat("--- regions containing more than one designated city ---\n")
print(as.data.frame(constituents |> filter(n > 1) |> dplyr::select(-`Region area (ha)`)),
      row.names = FALSE)

tryCatch({
  write.csv(constituents, file.path(figures_dir, "TableS1_city_constituents.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  library(officer)
  read_docx() |>
    body_add_par(paste0(
      "Table S1. Urban regions used for between-city comparison, and the ONS-designated ",
      "Major Towns and Cities each contains. Regions are delineated by continuity of built-up ",
      "land, so several absorb more than one designated city; connectivity values reported ",
      "against a region name describe the whole conurbation."), style = "Table Caption") |>
    body_add_table(as.data.frame(constituents), style = "Table Professional", first_row = TRUE) |>
    print(target = file.path(figures_dir, "TableS1_city_constituents.docx"))
  cat("\nWrote TableS1_city_constituents.csv and .docx\n")
}, error = function(e) warning("Could not write Table S1: ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE))
```

## Connectivity among England's cities

Reported in merged form, as above. Both the raw value and the
size-adjusted comparison are shown because they answer different
questions: the raw value says how much of the conurbation's woodland is
reachable, and the size-adjusted figure says whether it does better or
worse than places holding a comparable amount of woodland.

```{r city_leaderboard}
library(dplyr)
cities <- ok |> filter(region %in% city_regions, !is.na(ECS_pct_59))

# Size-adjusted score: divergence from the median of the k nearest
# regions by total woodland area, within the city set.
k <- 6
n <- nrow(cities); area <- cities$total_area_ha; pct <- cities$ECS_pct_59
div <- numeric(n)
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  dist <- abs(log(area) - log(area[i])); dist[i] <- Inf
  nn <- order(dist)[1:min(k, n - 1)]
  div[i] <- pct[i] - median(pct[nn])
}
cities$size_adjusted <- div

cat("=== Most connected (raw) ===\n")
print(cities |> arrange(desc(ECS_pct_59)) |>
        transmute(Region = region, `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
                  `Accessible at 59 m (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
                  `Size-adjusted` = round(size_adjusted, 3)) |> head(10), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Least connected (raw) ===\n")
print(cities |> arrange(ECS_pct_59) |>
        transmute(Region = region, `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
                  `Accessible at 59 m (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
                  `Size-adjusted` = round(size_adjusted, 3)) |> head(10), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Best and worst relative to comparably-wooded cities ===\n")
print(cities |> arrange(desc(size_adjusted)) |>
        transmute(Region = region, `Accessible (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
                  `Size-adjusted` = round(size_adjusted, 3)) |> head(5), row.names = FALSE)
print(cities |> arrange(size_adjusted) |>
        transmute(Region = region, `Accessible (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
                  `Size-adjusted` = round(size_adjusted, 3)) |> head(5), row.names = FALSE)

# Full lookup table for the supplement.
city_table <- cities |>
  arrange(desc(ECS_pct_59)) |>
  transmute(Region = region,
            `Region area (ha)` = format(round(area_ha), big.mark = ","),
            `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
            `Patches` = n_patches,
            `Accessible at 59 m (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
            `Accessible at 99 m (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_99, 1),
            `Size-adjusted (59 m)` = round(size_adjusted, 3))

```

## Most and least connected: a model-based leaderboard

Ranks regions by the residual of a model containing region area and
woodland amount (actual `ECS_pct` minus the model's expected `ECS_pct`
for a region of that size and woodland amount), replacing the kNN
peer-average approach above. Raw `ECS_pct` cannot be compared across
regions directly because it is confounded by both region area and
woodland amount, and the two confounds are not interchangeable: once
region area is controlled, the relationship between woodland amount and
connectivity reverses sign, so a region with more woodland for its
footprint is genuinely better connected. A single kNN match on woodland
amount alone (`city_leaderboard`, above) does not capture this. Fitting
both predictors jointly means a region only tops the leaderboard by doing
better than places like it, not by being small.

```{r national_leaderboard}
library(mgcv)
library(dplyr)

build_leaderboard <- function(pct_col, label, floor_ha = 10) {
  sub <- ok |> filter(total_area_ha >= floor_ha, !is.na(.data[[pct_col]]))
  sub$log_area_region <- log(sub$area_ha)
  sub$log_woodland <- log(sub$total_area_ha)

  m <- gam(reformulate(c("s(log_area_region, k = 5)", "s(log_woodland, k = 5)"), response = pct_col),
           data = sub, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")

  sub$expected_pct <- predict(m, type = "response")
  sub$divergence_pp <- 100 * (sub[[pct_col]] - sub$expected_pct)

  cat("\n===", label, "-- national (n =", nrow(sub), ", woodland floor", floor_ha, "ha) ===\n")
  cat("--- Most connected relative to expectation (top 15) ---\n")
  print(sub |> arrange(desc(divergence_pp)) |>
          transmute(Region = region, `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
                    `Region area (ha)` = round(area_ha, 0),
                    `Actual (%)` = round(100 * .data[[pct_col]], 1),
                    `Expected (%)` = round(100 * expected_pct, 1),
                    `Divergence (pp)` = round(divergence_pp, 1)) |> head(15),
        row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\n--- Least connected relative to expectation (bottom 15) ---\n")
  print(sub |> arrange(divergence_pp) |>
          transmute(Region = region, `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
                    `Region area (ha)` = round(area_ha, 0),
                    `Actual (%)` = round(100 * .data[[pct_col]], 1),
                    `Expected (%)` = round(100 * expected_pct, 1),
                    `Divergence (pp)` = round(divergence_pp, 1)) |> head(15),
        row.names = FALSE)

  city_sub <- sub |> filter(region %in% city_regions)
  cat("\n--- Named cities only: most connected relative to expectation (top 10 of",
      nrow(city_sub), ") ---\n")
  print(city_sub |> arrange(desc(divergence_pp)) |>
          transmute(Region = region, `Actual (%)` = round(100 * .data[[pct_col]], 1),
                    `Expected (%)` = round(100 * expected_pct, 1),
                    `Divergence (pp)` = round(divergence_pp, 1)) |> head(10),
        row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\n--- Named cities only: least connected relative to expectation (bottom 10) ---\n")
  print(city_sub |> arrange(divergence_pp) |>
          transmute(Region = region, `Actual (%)` = round(100 * .data[[pct_col]], 1),
                    `Expected (%)` = round(100 * expected_pct, 1),
                    `Divergence (pp)` = round(divergence_pp, 1)) |> head(10),
        row.names = FALSE)

  invisible(sub)
}

lb_59 <- build_leaderboard("ECS_pct_59", "59 m")
lb_99 <- build_leaderboard("ECS_pct_99", "99 m")

# How much city ranks shift between thresholds: a concrete illustration
# that "well connected" depends on the movement threshold, not only on the
# landscape.
shift <- lb_59 |> filter(region %in% city_regions) |>
  transmute(region, div_59 = divergence_pp) |>
  inner_join(lb_99 |> filter(region %in% city_regions) |>
               transmute(region, div_99 = divergence_pp),
             by = "region") |>
  mutate(rank_59 = rank(-div_59), rank_99 = rank(-div_99),
         rank_shift = rank_59 - rank_99) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rank_shift)))

cat("\n=== Cities whose rank shifts most between 59 m and 99 m ===\n")
print(shift |> transmute(Region = region, `Rank at 59m` = rank_59, `Rank at 99m` = rank_99,
                          `Rank shift` = rank_shift) |> head(10), row.names = FALSE)

tryCatch({
  write.csv(lb_59 |> arrange(desc(divergence_pp)) |>
              transmute(Region = region, `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
                        `Region area (ha)` = round(area_ha, 0),
                        `Accessible at 59 m (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),
                        `Expected at 59 m (%)` = round(100 * expected_pct, 1),
                        `Divergence at 59 m (pp)` = round(divergence_pp, 1)),
            file.path(figures_dir, "TableS3_national_leaderboard_59m.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nWrote TableS3_national_leaderboard_59m.csv (", nrow(lb_59), "regions )\n")
}, error = function(e) warning("Could not write Table S3: ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE))
```
